_doc: graph.sem data. min_coverage: the share of a package's definitions the SCIP index must define before it may refute a name edge. engines: per SCIP engine, no_refute = the reason its overlays never refute a name edge (checked on tests/fixtures/sem/union). max_index_bytes: a larger index.scip is not read. apply_bytes_per_s: how many bytes of an index.scip sem.refine applies per second (measured on synthetic indexes of 12 and 128 MB: 2.9 and 2.1 MB/s, one worker, so 2 MB/s); graph.semuse leaves out a cached index that would not be applied inside what is left of the budget (W dc.sem-budget). manifests: per language family, the files (besides the sources of the family) that are inputs of an index, so a changed go.mod or tsconfig makes the overlay stale. lsp: servers per family (engine and exe are names of data/engines.json; the path comes from the one engine resolver, never from the repository), max_queries per language, budget_s for all languages together, grace_s to wait for a server to announce its indexing, settle_s the most a server may hold a language's share of the budget while it finishes indexing; a server entry may carry needs_sandbox (it runs project code: build scripts, proc-macros, and writes into the tree: servers() does not offer it unless the caller says it runs in a sandbox) and init (its initializationOptions, e.g. {"tsserver": {"path": ...}} for typescript-language-server, which needs a tsserver of TypeScript 5 or older: with a newer typescript there is none, so JS and TS report W dc.sem-lsp-failed until one is installed).

scip-python.no_refute: scip-python 0.6.8 resolves a member access on a union type (x: A | B, Union[A, B]) to the first member only, so the index says nothing against the other members; it confirms, it does not refute
